```yaml
container:
```

This limit can be further reduced (but not increased) by the same option in a job.

body.title: Docs about pull request templates
body.body:
Hi, was told to move [this issue](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/website/issues/1142) here.

There is an undocumented feature with pull request templates, it will [add the content of the PR to fields with `id: body`](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/commit/acce8bbc3efd2aaa6ee9097d3d3d5e72e7de401f/routers/web/repo/compare.go#L835).

I can not find this feature [documented](https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/user/repository/issue-pull-request-templates/), but it works very nicely with just:
```yaml
  - type: textarea
    id: body
    attributes:
      label: Pull Request Description
```

The commit in `jelu-patch-2` is:
```
commit 169d81a82f850bbae982d9c5a89218424b740bc2 (origin/jelu-patch-2)
Author: jelu <jelu@noreply.codeberg.org>
Date:   Tue Oct 13 09:34:31 2026 +0200

    bla bla
    
    - bla
    - bla
```

body.title: Anecdotal first contribution experience
body.body:
# Background
I am new to go almost entirely but I am an experienced web dev (mostly scripting languages and databases) and 25+ of OSS experience as a contributor and in leadership

# The Experience

  I noticed that there were no counts on results in the repo/user/org/code search UI but there was pagination. So I figured the data must be available in some form. Note I just wanted a rough number at least. Didn’t have to be exact.

I checked out the source code and looked at https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/branch/forgejo/CONTRIBUTING.md  I was already aware of the AI related rules but found https://forgejo.org/docs/next/contributor/ there.

I figured this was likely just a template issue or at least from the pagination issue I could work my way back to where the relevant code was so I searched for “template” in the contributor docs.  

I didn’t find anything. So I looked at the designer section but it also didn’t look relevant. I did find https://forgejo.org/docs/next/contributor/customization/ which was helpful to learn about go templates

  I then decided to search the code itself. Which is how I found https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/branch/forgejo/templates/explore  

I am not sure how I then finally made my way to find https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/branch/forgejo/routers/web/explore

But once I did it was quite straightforward to find the “total” var for each of the cases and see how to pass it on to the template.

  I then went back to the contributor doc to find https://forgejo.org/docs/next/contributor/from-source/ and with a bit of fiddling and my experience with docker I was able to get a local dev setup.

  I then submitted a PR https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14147

I worked through the contributor template but wasn’t sure which sections applied to my PR since it was so seemingly trivial. I did notice the “First-time contributor” tag added to the PR and thought this could trigger some sort of “mentorship” process.

Shortly after I got the first feedback from mfenniak who said that he prefers not to pile things that could complicate future changes related to larger forgejo instances.  

I tried to address those concerns with a comment. And then with another comment a few days later. I then also reached out to aahlenst (I had some questions on matrix about forgejo where he helped me. I assume it helped that he knew my name from the PHP community) who then also commented and suggested I should take mfenniak to ask how to move forward.

A few days after that I decided to do just that and Mathieu responded again who addressed my feedback and agreed with aahlenst that a larger discussion is needed.

After my next reply aahlenst and I went back and forth a bit on how to solve the scalability concerns that mfenniak had raised.   But it is still unclear to me how this would become a larger discussion that mfenniak indicated was needed.

  I think sometime in this process I also went to the development channel but quickly realized that there were too many discussions going on for it to be feasible to try and bring up my relatively small PR. Let alone be able to keep up to see if someone would respond to me.

I have since been made aware of https://codeberg.org/forgejo/governance/src/branch/main/DECISION-MAKING.md while suggesting the PHP RFC process in the sustainability chat on Matrix.   —

# My key takeaways: 
* There is a lot of documentation for best practices, newcomers and processes but its so much that I admittedly didn’t attempt to read it all
* Having aahlenst support me was what gave me confidence that I should continue the discussion
* A dedicated channel for newcomers where one can find a mentor to work through the first few contributions would be amazing

body.title: Docker app.ini path misleading
body.body:
New user of forgejo here. It took me some time to find the `app.ini` file when running Forgejo with Docker.

The Docker installation documentation says that configuration is stored in `app.ini`, but does not specify where the file is:

https://codeberg.org/forgejo/docs/src/commit/55b68013c82b83212c59bbfc093d30d520789552/docs/admin/installation/docker.md?display=source#L105-L108

It links to the Configuration Cheat Sheet, which mentions `custom/conf/app.ini` and `/etc/forgejo/app.ini`:

https://codeberg.org/forgejo/docs/src/commit/55b68013c82b83212c59bbfc093d30d520789552/docs/admin/config-cheat-sheet.md?display=source#L10-L12

Neither path appears to be correct for the provided docker compose setup. In that case the file is found at:

`/data/gitea/conf/app.ini`

It would be helpful if the Docker setup documentation stated this path explicitly. The Configuration Cheat Sheet could also clarify that `/etc/forgejo/app.ini` applies to distribution or package installations, rather than the standard Docker image.

The following paragraph in the Docker documentation explains the `FORGEJO__[SECTION]__[KEY]` environment variables. However, it took me a while to understand the relationship between these variables and `app.ini`.

https://codeberg.org/forgejo/docs/src/commit/55b68013c82b83212c59bbfc093d30d520789552/docs/admin/installation/docker.md?display=source#L110-L112

As I understand it:

- `app.ini` is created automatically if it does not already exist
- Environment variables are written to the file
- Changing an environment variable updates the value
- Removing an environment variable does not remove the previously written value from `app.ini`

It might be clearer to describe this behavior explicitly, for example:

> When using the Forgejo container image, `/data/gitea/conf/app.ini` is automatically created if it does not already exist. The environment variables `FORGEJO__[SECTION]__[KEY]` values are automatically written in this file. But removing an environment variable does not remove its value from `app.ini`.

Also `It is possible` sounds a bit too much of an optional information and the reference Configuration Cheat Sheet is misleading at that point.

I hope this feedback on the documentation is helpful. I was quite confused.

body.title: Reverse proxy example kubernetes ingress
body.body:
I read the reverse proxy documentation, but missed the rewrite requirement. Maybe it would be good to mention it.
The nginx-ingress looks now like (if you want to add it):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: forgejo-ingress
  namespace: forgejo
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /$2
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/websocket-services: "forgejo"

spec:
  ingressClassName: public
  rules:
  - http:
      paths:
      - path: /forgejo(/|$)(.*)
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: forgejo
            port:
              number: 3000
```

_Originally posted by @th-2021 in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/issues/13241#issuecomment-18294092_
